name: targeted-1026-201334
hypothesis: Failure pattern: before the first promotion, the player gives Output away in stories for comfort or learning it does not need, just before a review that reads Output. The champion's only early exits (2 of its latest 12 games) are capability dismissals at month 24 by players who never left L1 in the first year. In its 6 digests every game promoted at the first or second review completed (4/4) and both games promoted at neither were dismissed (2/2). This matches the lab tally: first promotion at review 1, 12/14 completed; at review 2, 7/11; later, 0/13. The first promotion is legible in the digests. At the 10 first-year reviews held at L1, all 4 promotions came with Output and Network both at the highest value the game shows at L1, and all 6 misses had one of them below it. In all 6 misses both had reached that value after the last quarterly phase, and a story choice then took one away when no Energy phase was left to restore it before the review. In 3 of the 6, and in both early-exit games, the player gave Output away for something it was not short of. Three times it put work off for rest at Health 5 to 7: ladd-00001 review 1, scre-00004 review 2 and scre-00002 review 1. In scre-00004 that trade was the last decision before the review and the whole shortfall. Once it learned on the job with Skill already stalled (scre-00002 review 1; also scre-00003 review 1, where a later story happened to restore Output). The same rest trade preceded a missed first-window promotion in two Opus games of other policies: cali-dd49c06c-eaaedd-00000 (F3), dismissed at month 24, and cali-3207e8f5-a10402-00000, promoted only at review 2. The other misses came from honest disclosure choices, a courtesy note and a no-win side duty, which this change leaves alone. Why the champion does this: its story rules protect Health and Dignity and lift the weakest statistic, but say nothing about Output and Network before the first promotion, and Haiku cites Protect for Health at 7. Why the change fixes it: a story priority until the first promotion keeps Output and Network and forbids trading them for rest at comfortable Health or for learning once Skill has stalled. Rest moves to Health recovery in the next Energy phase, where at L1 points often go to Network maintenance on a Network that is not rising. More first-year reviews should then find both inputs at their high, converting some first-year misses into promotions and cutting month-24 dismissals. It differs from f7-delivery-stories-v1 (4 games, Q 46.5, not above its parent). That rule fired only once Output or Network was already below its recent high, after the loss. This rule guards both while they are at their high, names the losing trades, and sits below Protect and Risk so low-Health rest and honest disclosure still win.
change: Adds one story priority between Risk and Review (Review and Balance renumbered, their text unchanged): until the first promotion, keep Output and Network in stories and do not trade them for rest or exercise while Health is comfortable or for learning once Skill has stopped rising. If Health slips, recover it in the next Energy phase, and never hide or postpone a problem to keep them.
predicted_behaviour: Before the first promotion, story notes cite the First-promotion priority. With Health outside the lower part of its range, the player picks the option that keeps its own work moving over one that puts work off for rest or exercise, and declines on-the-job learning once Skill has stopped rising. Honest disclosure choices and rest choices at low Health are unchanged. Energy phases at L1 show Health recovery after Health dipped, in place of Network maintenance on a Network that is not rising. More first-year L1 reviews find Output and Network both at their high, more games are promoted at the first or second review, and month-24 dismissals fall below the champion's 2 in 12. Resilience in completed games stays near the champion's 100, with no blackout. After the first promotion, play is the champion's.
refutation: Refuted if, over 8 or more race games, completion is not above the champion's 10 of 12 and month-24 dismissals do not fall, or if a blackout or Health-driven exit appears (champion 0 of 12), or if the mean score is below the champion's by more than the decision margin. The mechanism is refuted if notes show these trades declined and first-year L1 reviews with Output and Network at their high still miss promotion. Uninformative if, before the first promotion, the player still puts work off for rest at comfortable Health or learns on the job with Skill stalled; then the rule was not executed.
